## Synthesis: This feature already exists — issue #2 is largely already implemented

**The single most important finding:** per-account "Export as CSV" already exists end-to-end, and has existed since the initial open-source commit (`4d9fdfc59`) — it's not new code. It's just tucked inside the account's "⋮" (three-dot) overflow menu rather than a visible toolbar button, which is almost certainly why the issue author didn't find it.

### 1. Budget-level export vs. existing CSV logic
- Budget-level export: `packages/desktop-client/src/components/settings/Export.tsx:22-43` — calls `send('export-budget')`, handled by `packages/loot-core/src/server/budgetfiles/app.ts:67,91`. This exports a **zip** (`db.sqlite` + `metadata.json`), not CSV — a different, unrelated code path.
- The actual CSV logic is in `packages/loot-core/src/server/transactions/export/export-to-csv.ts`:
  - `exportToCSV()` (line 17) — takes a raw transaction list.
  - `exportQueryToCSV(query)` (line 69) — takes an AQL `Query`, runs `aqlQuery`, handles split transactions, and produces CSV via `csv-stringify`. This is the one used by the account view.
  - Wired up in `packages/loot-core/src/server/transactions/app.ts:109-129` as handlers `transactions-export` and `transactions-export-query` (called by client via `send('transactions-export-query', {...})`).
- This is fully reusable — nothing new needs to be written for serialization.

### 2. Account view / toolbar file
- `packages/desktop-client/src/components/accounts/Header.tsx` renders the toolbar (`AccountHeader`, line 135) with Search, FilterButton, SelectedTransactionsButton, Reconcile, etc. (lines 340-566).
- The account "⋮" menu is `AccountMenu` (line 762) inside `Header.tsx`, which already lists `{ name: 'export', text: t('Export') }` at **line 819** (and again at line 552 for the "all accounts" view).
- Selecting it calls `onMenuSelect` in `packages/desktop-client/src/components/accounts/Account.tsx:799-855`, case `'export'` (line 852-855) → `this.onExport(accountName)` (defined lines 642-655).
- `onExport` calls `send('transactions-export-query', { query: this.currentQuery.serialize() })`, builds a filename, and calls `window.Actual.saveFile(...)`.
- **This is exactly where a "Download as CSV" button would go** — either promote this existing menu item to a bare `Button` in `AccountHeader`'s `SpaceBetween` toolbar row (`Header.tsx:340-566`, alongside Import/Add New/FilterButton), or simply relabel/re-icon the existing menu entry.

### 3. Data access and filter edge case — a real gap found
- Transaction list is **not** a fully-loaded client-side array; it's a `pagedQuery` (`packages/desktop-client/src/components/accounts/Account.tsx:85-86, 300, 483`), i.e., virtualized/paginated. Export correctly avoids depending on that in-memory page and instead re-runs a query server-side via `transactions-export-query`.
- Filter state: `this.currentQuery` starts as `this.rootQuery` (line 454) and gets reassigned when the rule-based `FilterButton`/`applyFilters` is used (line 1565: `this.currentQuery = this.rootQuery.filter(...)`), so **exporting after applying a saved/rule filter correctly narrows the CSV**.
- **However**, the free-text `Search` box does NOT update `this.currentQuery`. In `onSearchDone` (lines 580-596), the search-derived query (`queries.transactionsSearch(this.currentQuery, this.state.search, ...)`) is passed straight to `updateQuery` for the on-screen paged list only — it is never assigned back to `this.currentQuery`. Since `onExport` (line 644) serializes `this.currentQuery`, **a search term typed into the box is silently ignored by Export** — the exported CSV will contain the full (or rule-filtered) account, not just the visibly-searched rows. This is precisely the "filtered vs. full account" edge case the issue calls out, and it's a pre-existing latent bug/gap in the current export path, not something new to invent — worth deciding explicitly whether the new work should fix it (e.g., include search text when serializing the query) or explicitly document the limitation.

### 4. Reusable UI/file-save primitives
- `window.Actual.saveFile(contents, filename, title?)` is the shared save primitive, implemented for browser in `packages/desktop-client/src/browser-preload.js:187-195` (creates a `Blob`, triggers an `<a download>` click) and used identically in four places: `settings/Export.tsx:36`, `accounts/Account.tsx:650`, `reports/Overview.tsx:336`, `reports/reports/BudgetAnalysis.tsx:338`. Any new button reuses this unchanged.
- Icon: `SvgDownloadThickBottom` (`@actual-app/components/icons/v2`) is already imported in `Header.tsx:16` and used for the "Import" button — same icon family fits a "Download CSV" button visually.

### 5. Risk assessment
**Low risk.** This is not a new feature touching shared/critical paths — it's exposing/relocating an already-battle-tested, already-shipped code path:
- No changes needed to the transaction data layer, sync logic, or DB layer.
- No new server handler needed (`transactions-export-query` already exists and is stable, used since initial commit).
- The only genuinely new work is UI: adding/promoting a button in `Header.tsx`'s toolbar and wiring its `onPress` to the existing `onExport`/`onMenuSelect('export')` path in `Account.tsx`.
- The one substantive design decision (not a risky code change, but a product decision) is whether to fix the search-term gap described in #3 — that would mean also serializing/including `this.state.search` when building the exported query, a small, isolated change localized to `onExport`/`currentQuery` handling in `Account.tsx`, not touching sync or storage.

**Time estimate implication:** given the backend and even the account-level trigger already exist, this is much smaller than "scope: medium" for a from-scratch CSV export — realistically a small UI relocation/polish task, plus optionally a small fix for the search-filter edge case. Worth flagging to the issue reporter/maintainers that the core ask may already be resolved, and the real remaining work is discoverability (button placement) and the search-filter consistency fix.

8

33	      );

35	    },

37	  );

69	export async function exportQueryToCSV(query) {
70	  const { data: transactions } = await aqlQuery(
71	    query
72	      .select([
73	        { Id: 'id' },
74	        { Account: 'account.name' },
75	        { Date: 'date' },
76	        { Payee: 'payee.name' },
77	        { ParentId: 'parent_id' },
78	        { IsParent: 'is_parent' },
79	        { IsChild: 'is_child' },
80	        { SortOrder: 'sort_order' },
81	        { Notes: 'notes' },
82	        { CategoryGroup: 'category.group.name' },
83	        { Category: 'category.name' },
84	        { Amount: 'amount' },
85	        { Cleared: 'cleared' },
86	        { Reconciled: 'reconciled' },
87	      ])
88	      .options({ splits: 'all' }),
89	  );
90	
91	  // initialize a map to allow splits to have correct number of split from
92	  const parentsChildCount: Map<number, number> = new Map();
93	  const childSplitOrder: Map<number, number> = new Map();
94	
95	  // find children, their order, and total # siblings
96	  for (const trans of transactions) {
97	    if (trans.IsChild) {
98	      let childNumber = parentsChildCount.get(trans.ParentId) || 0;
99	      childNumber++;
100	      childSplitOrder.set(trans.Id, childNumber);
101	      parentsChildCount.set(trans.ParentId, childNumber);
102	    }
103	  }
104	
105	  // map final properties for export and grab the child count for splits from their parent transaction
106	  const transactionsForExport = transactions.map(trans => {
107	    return {
108	      Account: trans.Account,
109	      Date: trans.Date,
110	      Payee: trans.Payee,
111	      Notes: trans.IsParent
112	        ? '(SPLIT INTO ' +
113	          parentsChildCount.get(trans.Id) +
114	          ') ' +
115	          (trans.Notes || '')
116	        : trans.IsChild
117	          ? '(SPLIT ' +
118	            childSplitOrder.get(trans.Id) +
119	            ' OF ' +
120	            parentsChildCount.get(trans.ParentId) +
121	            ') ' +
122	            (trans.Notes || '')
123	          : trans.Notes,
124	      Category_Group: trans.CategoryGroup,
125	      Category: trans.Category,
126	      Amount: trans.IsParent
127	        ? 0
128	        : trans.Amount == null
129	          ? 0
130	          : integerToAmount(trans.Amount),
131	      Split_Amount: trans.IsParent ? integerToAmount(trans.Amount) : 0,
132	      Cleared:
133	        trans.Reconciled === true
134	          ? 'Reconciled'
135	          : trans.Cleared === true
136	            ? 'Cleared'
137	            : 'Not cleared',
138	    };
139	  });
140

I now have everything needed. Here's the concise report.

## Synthesis: This feature already exists — issue #2 is largely already implemented

**The single most important finding:** per-account "Export as CSV" already exists end-to-end, and has existed since the initial open-source commit (`4d9fdfc59`) — it's not new code. It's just tucked inside the account's "⋮" (three-dot) overflow menu rather than a visible toolbar button, which is almost certainly why the issue author didn't find it.

### 1. Budget-level export vs. existing CSV logic
- Budget-level export: `packages/desktop-client/src/components/settings/Export.tsx:22-43` — calls `send('export-budget')`, handled by `packages/loot-core/src/server/budgetfiles/app.ts:67,91`. This exports a **zip** (`db.sqlite` + `metadata.json`), not CSV — a different, unrelated code path.
- The actual CSV logic is in `packages/loot-core/src/server/transactions/export/export-to-csv.ts`:
  - `exportToCSV()` (line 17) — takes a raw transaction list.
  - `exportQueryToCSV(query)` (line 69) — takes an AQL `Query`, runs `aqlQuery`, handles split transactions, and produces CSV via `csv-stringify`. This is the one used by the account view.
  - Wired up in `packages/loot-core/src/server/transactions/app.ts:109-129` as handlers `transactions-export` and `transactions-export-query` (called by client via `send('transactions-export-query', {...})`).
- This is fully reusable — nothing new needs to be written for serialization.

### 2. Account view / toolbar file
- `packages/desktop-client/src/components/accounts/Header.tsx` renders the toolbar (`AccountHeader`, line 135) with Search, FilterButton, SelectedTransactionsButton, Reconcile, etc. (lines 340-566).
- The account "⋮" menu is `AccountMenu` (line 762) inside `Header.tsx`, which already lists `{ name: 'export', text: t('Export') }` at **line 819** (and again at line 552 for the "all accounts" view).
- Selecting it calls `onMenuSelect` in `packages/desktop-client/src/components/accounts/Account.tsx:799-855`, case `'export'` (line 852-855) → `this.onExport(accountName)` (defined lines 642-655).
- `onExport` calls `send('transactions-export-query', { query: this.currentQuery.serialize() })`, builds a filename, and calls `window.Actual.saveFile(...)`.
- **This is exactly where a "Download as CSV" button would go** — either promote this existing menu item to a bare `Button` in `AccountHeader`'s `SpaceBetween` toolbar row (`Header.tsx:340-566`, alongside Import/Add New/FilterButton), or simply relabel/re-icon the existing menu entry.

### 3. Data access and filter edge case — a real gap found
- Transaction list is **not** a fully-loaded client-side array; it's a `pagedQuery` (`packages/desktop-client/src/components/accounts/Account.tsx:85-86, 300, 483`), i.e., virtualized/paginated. Export correctly avoids depending on that in-memory page and instead re-runs a query server-side via `transactions-export-query`.
- Filter state: `this.currentQuery` starts as `this.rootQuery` (line 454) and gets reassigned when the rule-based `FilterButton`/`applyFilters` is used (line 1565: `this.currentQuery = this.rootQuery.filter(...)`), so **exporting after applying a saved/rule filter correctly narrows the CSV**.
- **However**, the free-text `Search` box does NOT update `this.currentQuery`. In `onSearchDone` (lines 580-596), the search-derived query (`queries.transactionsSearch(this.currentQuery, this.state.search, ...)`) is passed straight to `updateQuery` for the on-screen paged list only — it is never assigned back to `this.currentQuery`. Since `onExport` (line 644) serializes `this.currentQuery`, **a search term typed into the box is silently ignored by Export** — the exported CSV will contain the full (or rule-filtered) account, not just the visibly-searched rows. This is precisely the "filtered vs. full account" edge case the issue calls out, and it's a pre-existing latent bug/gap in the current export path, not something new to invent — worth deciding explicitly whether the new work should fix it (e.g., include search text when serializing the query) or explicitly document the limitation.

### 4. Reusable UI/file-save primitives
- `window.Actual.saveFile(contents, filename, title?)` is the shared save primitive, implemented for browser in `packages/desktop-client/src/browser-preload.js:187-195` (creates a `Blob`, triggers an `<a download>` click) and used identically in four places: `settings/Export.tsx:36`, `accounts/Account.tsx:650`, `reports/Overview.tsx:336`, `reports/reports/BudgetAnalysis.tsx:338`. Any new button reuses this unchanged.
- Icon: `SvgDownloadThickBottom` (`@actual-app/components/icons/v2`) is already imported in `Header.tsx:16` and used for the "Import" button — same icon family fits a "Download CSV" button visually.

### 5. Risk assessment
**Low risk.** This is not a new feature touching shared/critical paths — it's exposing/relocating an already-battle-tested, already-shipped code path:
- No changes needed to the transaction data layer, sync logic, or DB layer.
- No new server handler needed (`transactions-export-query` already exists and is stable, used since initial commit).
- The only genuinely new work is UI: adding/promoting a button in `Header.tsx`'s toolbar and wiring its `onPress` to the existing `onExport`/`onMenuSelect('export')` path in `Account.tsx`.
- The one substantive design decision (not a risky code change, but a product decision) is whether to fix the search-term gap described in #3 — that would mean also serializing/including `this.state.search` when building the exported query, a small, isolated change localized to `onExport`/`currentQuery` handling in `Account.tsx`, not touching sync or storage.

**Time estimate implication:** given the backend and even the account-level trigger already exist, this is much smaller than "scope: medium" for a from-scratch CSV export — realistically a small UI relocation/polish task, plus optionally a small fix for the search-filter edge case. Worth flagging to the issue reporter/maintainers that the core ask may already be resolved, and the real remaining work is discoverability (button placement) and the search-filter consistency fix.

## Summary of Findings

### 1. Where months are displayed & where arrow-key navigation lives

**`packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/DynamicBudgetTable.tsx`** is the load-bearing file:

- Lines 86–96: `useHotkeys('left', ...)` → calls `_onMonthSelect(monthUtils.prevMonth(startMonth))`
- Lines 97–107: `useHotkeys('right', ...)` → calls `_onMonthSelect(monthUtils.nextMonth(startMonth))`
- Lines 108–127: `useHotkeys('0', ...)` → jumps to current month (same pattern)
- Lines 82–84: `_onMonthSelect(month)` — a single local wrapper function that clamps the target month to valid bounds (via `getValidMonth`, lines 70–80) and calls the `onMonthSelect` prop with `(validMonth, numMonths)`
- Line 156: that same `_onMonthSelect` is passed down as the `onMonthSelect` prop to `BudgetPageHeader`

Uses `react-hotkeys-hook` (`scopes: ['app']`), not a raw `keydown` listener — worth knowing since a wheel handler would be a plain DOM/React `onWheel` prop instead, a different mechanism but wired into the same `_onMonthSelect` call.

Number of months shown side-by-side is already dynamic: `getNumPossibleMonths(width, categoryWidth)` (lines 19–35) computes 1–6 months based on available width, clamped by a `maxMonths` pref.

### 2. What drives which month(s) are shown — single vs. multi-month state

It's a **single `startMonth` value**, centralized as a local pref:

- **`packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/index.tsx`**
  - Line 46: `const [startMonthPref, setStartMonthPref] = useLocalPref('budget.startMonth');`
  - Line 47: `const startMonth = startMonthPref || currentMonth;`
  - Lines 87–117: `onMonthSelect(month, numDisplayed)` — calls `setStartMonthPref(month)` and does some prewarming heuristics; this is the ultimate state setter for the whole page.

`numMonths` (how many months are visible starting at `startMonth`) is a derived, computed value (from viewport width), not independent state — so "showing multiple months" is a windowing effect over one `startMonth` anchor, not multiple independently-selected months.

Click-to-select flow: **`packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/MonthPicker.tsx`**
- Line 96: "Today" button → `onSelect(currentMonth)`
- Line 114: prev chevron → `onSelect(monthUtils.prevMonth(startMonth))`
- Line 214: clicking a month cell → `onSelect(month)`
- Line 243: next chevron → `onSelect(monthUtils.nextMonth(startMonth))`

`onSelect` is wired through **`packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/BudgetPageHeader.tsx`** line 43 (`onSelect={month => onMonthSelect(month)}`) straight back to `_onMonthSelect` in `DynamicBudgetTable.tsx`.

So arrow keys, the prev/next chevron buttons, clicking a month cell, and the "Today" button are **already all the same code path**: `_onMonthSelect` → `onMonthSelect` prop → `setStartMonthPref` in `index.tsx`.

### 3. Existing wheel/scroll handling to use as reference

Searched the whole repo (`grep -rn "onWheel\|addEventListener('wheel'"`): the **only** hit is `packages/desktop-client/src/components/formula/codeMirror-excelLanguage.tsx` (lines 1098, 1113), which is CodeMirror's own scroll-zoom-prevention plumbing for the formula editor — unrelated and not a useful UX reference. **There is no existing wheel-to-navigate pattern anywhere in the codebase** (not in reports, not in any date/calendar picker). This would be a net-new interaction pattern, not an extension of an established one.

### 4. Centralized vs. scattered — implementation risk

**Centralized, low risk.** Every existing month-navigation trigger (arrow keys, prev/next buttons, clicking a month cell, "Today" button) already funnels into the single `_onMonthSelect` function in `DynamicBudgetTable.tsx` (lines 82–84), which in turn calls the one `setStartMonthPref` state setter in `index.tsx` (lines 87–117, which also handles prewarming/bounds-clamping). A wheel handler added to `BudgetPageHeader`/`MonthPicker` (or `DynamicBudgetTable`) would just need to call the same `_onMonthSelect(monthUtils.prevMonth(startMonth))` / `nextMonth(...)` — reusing all existing bounds-clamping (`getValidMonth`) and cache-prewarming logic for free. No duplicated state to keep in sync.

The only "new" design decision is translating wheel-delta into discrete month steps (throttling/debouncing so one scroll gesture doesn't fire dozens of month changes) — that's genuinely new logic, not reuse of an existing pattern, which is likely what the issue means by the input being "more difficult" than it looks.

### 5. Risk of conflicting with normal scroll behavior

Low, due to DOM layout separation in **`packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/BudgetTable.tsx`**:

- Lines 264–284: the month-summary header row (`MonthsProvider` + `BudgetSummaries`) sits in a `View` with `overflow: 'hidden'`, `flexShrink: 0` — it is not scrollable itself.
- Lines 297–306: the actual category grid lives in a separate `View` (`ref={scrollContainerRef}`, `data-testid="budget-table-scroll-container"`) with `overflowY: 'scroll'` — this is the vertically-scrollable element, and it's a distinct DOM subtree from the month header/picker.
- `BudgetPageHeader`/`MonthPicker` (rendered above `BudgetTable` in `DynamicBudgetTable.tsx` line 152–157) is yet another separate, non-scrolling element.

So an `onWheel` handler scoped to the `MonthPicker`/`BudgetPageHeader` area would not sit on top of, or share an element with, the vertically-scrolling category grid — attaching it there shouldn't hijack the grid's normal scroll. The main residual risk is UX rather than technical breakage: if a user's trackpad/mouse wheel produces vertical scroll deltas while hovering over the header (which has nothing to scroll), interpreting any wheel event there as "change month" could feel surprising unless the handler is deliberately restricted (e.g., only reacts past some threshold, or only to horizontal delta/shift+wheel, matching common calendar-scroll conventions) and calls `preventDefault` narrowly. No sibling reference pattern exists in-repo for this threshold/debounce logic (per point 3), so that part should be treated as new, hand-designed logic and tested carefully, even though the state wiring itself is simple and centralized.

1	// @ts-strict-ignore
2	import React, { createContext } from 'react';
3	import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
4	
5	import * as monthUtils from '@actual-app/core/shared/months';
6	
7	export type MonthBounds = {
8	  start: string;
9	  end: string;
10	};
11	
12	export function getValidMonthBounds(
13	  bounds: MonthBounds,
14	  startMonth: undefined | string,
15	  endMonth: string,
16	) {
17	  return {
18	    start: startMonth < bounds.start ? bounds.start : startMonth,
19	    end: endMonth > bounds.end ? bounds.end : endMonth,
20	  };
21	}
22	
23	type MonthsContextProps = {
24	  months: string[];
25	  type: string;
26	};
27	
28	export const MonthsContext = createContext<MonthsContextProps>(null);
29	
30	type MonthsProviderProps = {
31	  startMonth: string | undefined;
32	  numMonths: number;
33	  monthBounds: MonthBounds;
34	  type: string;
35	  children: ReactNode;
36	};
37	
38	export function MonthsProvider({
39	  startMonth,
40	  numMonths,
41	  monthBounds,
42	  type,
43	  children,
44	}: MonthsProviderProps) {
45	  const endMonth = monthUtils.addMonths(startMonth, numMonths - 1);
46	  const bounds = getValidMonthBounds(monthBounds, startMonth, endMonth);
47	  const months = monthUtils.rangeInclusive(bounds.start, bounds.end);
48	
49	  return (
50	    <MonthsContext.Provider value={{ months, type }}>
51	      {children}
52	    </MonthsContext.Provider>
53	  );
54	}
55

19	function getNumPossibleMonths(width: number, categoryWidth: number) {
20	  const estimatedTableWidth = width - categoryWidth;
21	
22	  if (estimatedTableWidth < 500) {
23	    return 1;
24	  } else if (estimatedTableWidth < 750) {
25	    return 2;
26	  } else if (estimatedTableWidth < 1000) {
27	    return 3;
28	  } else if (estimatedTableWidth < 1250) {
29	    return 4;
30	  } else if (estimatedTableWidth < 1500) {
31	    return 5;
32	  }
33	
34	  return 6;
35	}
36	
37	type DynamicBudgetTableProps = {
38	  width: number;
39	  height: number;
40	} & AutoSizingBudgetTableProps;
41	
42	const DynamicBudgetTable = ({
43	  type,
44	  width,
45	  height,
46	  prewarmStartMonth,
47	  startMonth,
48	  maxMonths = 3,
49	  monthBounds,
50	  onMonthSelect,
51	  onBudgetAction,
52	  ...props
53	}: DynamicBudgetTableProps) => {
54	  const { setDisplayMax } = useBudgetMonthCount();
55	  const [categoryExpandedStatePref] = useGlobalPref('categoryExpandedState');
56	  const isGoalTemplatesEnabled = useFeatureFlag('goalTemplatesEnabled');
57	  const categoryExpandedState = categoryExpandedStatePref ?? 0;
58	
59	  const numPossible = getNumPossibleMonths(
60	    width,
61	    200 + 100 * categoryExpandedState,
62	  );
63	  const numMonths = Math.min(numPossible, maxMonths);
64	  const maxWidth = 200 + 100 * categoryExpandedState + 500 * numMonths;
65	
66	  useEffect(() => {
67	    setDisplayMax(numPossible);
68	  }, [setDisplayMax, numPossible]);
69	
70	  function getValidMonth(month) {
71	    const start = monthBounds.start;
72	    const end = monthUtils.subMonths(monthBounds.end, numMonths - 1);
73	
74	    if (month < start) {
75	      return start;
76	    } else if (month > end) {
77	      return end;
78	    }
79	    return month;
80	  }
81	
82	  function _onMonthSelect(month) {
83	    onMonthSelect(getValidMonth(month), numMonths);
84	  }
85	
86	  useHotkeys(
87	    'left',
88	    () => {
89	      _onMonthSelect(monthUtils.prevMonth(startMonth));
90	    },
91	    {
92	      preventDefault: true,
93	      scopes: ['app'],
94	    },
95	    [_onMonthSelect, startMonth],
96	  );
97	  useHotkeys(
98	    'right',
99	    () => {
100	      _onMonthSelect(monthUtils.nextMonth(startMonth));
101	    },
102	    {
103	      preventDefault: true,
104	      scopes: ['app'],
105	    },
106	    [_onMonthSelect, startMonth],
107	  );
108	  useHotkeys(

114	          type === 'envelope'
115	            ? Math.floor((numMonths - 1) / 2)

137	    },
138	    [onBudgetAction, startMonth, isGoalTemplatesEnabled],
139	  );

141	  return (

156	            onMonthSelect={_onMonthSelect}
157	          />

163	            monthBounds={monthBounds}

## Summary of Findings

### 1. Where months are displayed & where arrow-key navigation lives

**`packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/DynamicBudgetTable.tsx`** is the load-bearing file:

- Lines 86–96: `useHotkeys('left', ...)` → calls `_onMonthSelect(monthUtils.prevMonth(startMonth))`
- Lines 97–107: `useHotkeys('right', ...)` → calls `_onMonthSelect(monthUtils.nextMonth(startMonth))`
- Lines 108–127: `useHotkeys('0', ...)` → jumps to current month (same pattern)
- Lines 82–84: `_onMonthSelect(month)` — a single local wrapper function that clamps the target month to valid bounds (via `getValidMonth`, lines 70–80) and calls the `onMonthSelect` prop with `(validMonth, numMonths)`
- Line 156: that same `_onMonthSelect` is passed down as the `onMonthSelect` prop to `BudgetPageHeader`

Uses `react-hotkeys-hook` (`scopes: ['app']`), not a raw `keydown` listener — worth knowing since a wheel handler would be a plain DOM/React `onWheel` prop instead, a different mechanism but wired into the same `_onMonthSelect` call.

Number of months shown side-by-side is already dynamic: `getNumPossibleMonths(width, categoryWidth)` (lines 19–35) computes 1–6 months based on available width, clamped by a `maxMonths` pref.

### 2. What drives which month(s) are shown — single vs. multi-month state

It's a **single `startMonth` value**, centralized as a local pref:

- **`packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/index.tsx`**
  - Line 46: `const [startMonthPref, setStartMonthPref] = useLocalPref('budget.startMonth');`
  - Line 47: `const startMonth = startMonthPref || currentMonth;`
  - Lines 87–117: `onMonthSelect(month, numDisplayed)` — calls `setStartMonthPref(month)` and does some prewarming heuristics; this is the ultimate state setter for the whole page.

`numMonths` (how many months are visible starting at `startMonth`) is a derived, computed value (from viewport width), not independent state — so "showing multiple months" is a windowing effect over one `startMonth` anchor, not multiple independently-selected months.

Click-to-select flow: **`packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/MonthPicker.tsx`**
- Line 96: "Today" button → `onSelect(currentMonth)`
- Line 114: prev chevron → `onSelect(monthUtils.prevMonth(startMonth))`
- Line 214: clicking a month cell → `onSelect(month)`
- Line 243: next chevron → `onSelect(monthUtils.nextMonth(startMonth))`

`onSelect` is wired through **`packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/BudgetPageHeader.tsx`** line 43 (`onSelect={month => onMonthSelect(month)}`) straight back to `_onMonthSelect` in `DynamicBudgetTable.tsx`.

So arrow keys, the prev/next chevron buttons, clicking a month cell, and the "Today" button are **already all the same code path**: `_onMonthSelect` → `onMonthSelect` prop → `setStartMonthPref` in `index.tsx`.

### 3. Existing wheel/scroll handling to use as reference

Searched the whole repo (`grep -rn "onWheel\|addEventListener('wheel'"`): the **only** hit is `packages/desktop-client/src/components/formula/codeMirror-excelLanguage.tsx` (lines 1098, 1113), which is CodeMirror's own scroll-zoom-prevention plumbing for the formula editor — unrelated and not a useful UX reference. **There is no existing wheel-to-navigate pattern anywhere in the codebase** (not in reports, not in any date/calendar picker). This would be a net-new interaction pattern, not an extension of an established one.

### 4. Centralized vs. scattered — implementation risk

**Centralized, low risk.** Every existing month-navigation trigger (arrow keys, prev/next buttons, clicking a month cell, "Today" button) already funnels into the single `_onMonthSelect` function in `DynamicBudgetTable.tsx` (lines 82–84), which in turn calls the one `setStartMonthPref` state setter in `index.tsx` (lines 87–117, which also handles prewarming/bounds-clamping). A wheel handler added to `BudgetPageHeader`/`MonthPicker` (or `DynamicBudgetTable`) would just need to call the same `_onMonthSelect(monthUtils.prevMonth(startMonth))` / `nextMonth(...)` — reusing all existing bounds-clamping (`getValidMonth`) and cache-prewarming logic for free. No duplicated state to keep in sync.

The only "new" design decision is translating wheel-delta into discrete month steps (throttling/debouncing so one scroll gesture doesn't fire dozens of month changes) — that's genuinely new logic, not reuse of an existing pattern, which is likely what the issue means by the input being "more difficult" than it looks.

### 5. Risk of conflicting with normal scroll behavior

Low, due to DOM layout separation in **`packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/BudgetTable.tsx`**:

- Lines 264–284: the month-summary header row (`MonthsProvider` + `BudgetSummaries`) sits in a `View` with `overflow: 'hidden'`, `flexShrink: 0` — it is not scrollable itself.
- Lines 297–306: the actual category grid lives in a separate `View` (`ref={scrollContainerRef}`, `data-testid="budget-table-scroll-container"`) with `overflowY: 'scroll'` — this is the vertically-scrollable element, and it's a distinct DOM subtree from the month header/picker.
- `BudgetPageHeader`/`MonthPicker` (rendered above `BudgetTable` in `DynamicBudgetTable.tsx` line 152–157) is yet another separate, non-scrolling element.

So an `onWheel` handler scoped to the `MonthPicker`/`BudgetPageHeader` area would not sit on top of, or share an element with, the vertically-scrolling category grid — attaching it there shouldn't hijack the grid's normal scroll. The main residual risk is UX rather than technical breakage: if a user's trackpad/mouse wheel produces vertical scroll deltas while hovering over the header (which has nothing to scroll), interpreting any wheel event there as "change month" could feel surprising unless the handler is deliberately restricted (e.g., only reacts past some threshold, or only to horizontal delta/shift+wheel, matching common calendar-scroll conventions) and calls `preventDefault` narrowly. No sibling reference pattern exists in-repo for this threshold/debounce logic (per point 3), so that part should be treated as new, hand-designed logic and tested carefully, even though the state wiring itself is simple and centralized.

So a wheel handler would just need to call the **same**
`_onMonthSelect(monthUtils.prevMonth/nextMonth(startMonth))` — reusing all
existing bounds-clamping and cache-prewarming for free. No duplicated state
to keep in sync, no changes needed to the data layer or sync logic.

**What's genuinely new:** there is no existing wheel/scroll-to-navigate
pattern anywhere in the codebase to extend (repo-wide `onWheel` search only
turns up unrelated CodeMirror zoom-prevention code in
`components/formula/codeMirror-excelLanguage.tsx`). Translating wheel-delta
into discrete month steps — with throttling/debouncing so one scroll gesture
doesn't fire dozens of month changes — is genuinely new, hand-designed logic.
This is almost certainly what the issue author meant by "may prove more
difficult."

**Scroll-conflict risk is low**, due to DOM separation in
`packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/BudgetTable.tsx`:

- Lines 264-284: the month header row (`MonthsProvider`/`BudgetSummaries`)
  has `overflow: 'hidden'`, `flexShrink: 0` — not scrollable itself.
- Lines 297-306: the category grid (`overflowY: 'scroll'`,
  `data-testid="budget-table-scroll-container"`) is a separate DOM subtree.
- `BudgetPageHeader`/`MonthPicker` sit above `BudgetTable`
  (`DynamicBudgetTable.tsx:152-157`), in yet another non-scrolling element.

A wheel handler scoped to the header/`MonthPicker` area wouldn't sit on top
of the vertically-scrolling grid, so it shouldn't hijack normal page scroll.
The residual risk is UX, not breakage: a wheel event over a non-scrolling
header could feel surprising unless scoped carefully (e.g. horizontal delta
only, or a deliberate threshold) — worth designing intentionally since there's
no in-repo convention to copy.

### Answer to the user's question

- **Time**: small-to-medium, leaning small. State wiring is trivial (reuse
  `_onMonthSelect`, already shared by every other navigation trigger). The
  only real work is: (a) adding an `onWheel` handler to the month
  header/`MonthPicker` area, (b) translating wheel delta into discrete
  month-step calls with reasonable debounce/threshold tuning (genuinely new,
  no reference pattern in-repo), and (c) manual testing across
  trackpad/mouse-wheel behavior since there's nothing existing to lean on for
  "feel."
- **Risk of breaking other things**: low. No changes needed to month-state
  management, the data layer, or sync logic — this plugs into the existing
  centralized `_onMonthSelect` path. DOM layout already separates the
  scrollable category grid from the non-scrolling header, so a wheel
  listener there is unlikely to interfere with normal vertical scrolling.
  Main risk is UX polish (feel of the debounce/threshold), not correctness
  or regression risk elsewhere.

3	import type { ReactNode } from 'react';

5	import * as monthUtils from '@actual-app/core/shared/months';
6	
7	export type MonthBounds = {
8	  start: string;
9	  end: string;
10	};
11	
12	export function getValidMonthBounds(
13	  bounds: MonthBounds,
14	  startMonth: undefined | string,
15	  endMonth: string,
16	) {
17	  return {
18	    start: startMonth < bounds.start ? bounds.start : startMonth,
19	    end: endMonth > bounds.end ? bounds.end : endMonth,
20	  };
21	}
22	
23	type MonthsContextProps = {
24	  months: string[];
25	  type: string;
26	};
27	
28	export const MonthsContext = createContext<MonthsContextProps>(null);
29	
30	type MonthsProviderProps = {
31	  startMonth: string | undefined;
32	  numMonths: number;
33	  monthBounds: MonthBounds;
34	  type: string;
35	  children: ReactNode;
36	};
37	
38	export function MonthsProvider({
39	  startMonth,
40	  numMonths,
41	  monthBounds,
42	  type,
43	  children,
44	}: MonthsProviderProps) {
45	  const endMonth = monthUtils.addMonths(startMonth, numMonths - 1);
46	  const bounds = getValidMonthBounds(monthBounds, startMonth, endMonth);
47	  const months = monthUtils.rangeInclusive(bounds.start, bounds.end);
48	
49	  return (
50	    <MonthsContext.Provider value={{ months, type }}>
51	      {children}
52	    </MonthsContext.Provider>
53	  );
54	}
55
```
</details></tool-use>

Why does it accumulate? Like if i do a long swipe, it switches between months but doesn't stop. I want it to stop when I've stopped moving the trackpad

---

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-13 17:19:00Z)**_

The issue is trackpad momentum: after you lift your fingers, macOS keeps firing wheel events with decaying deltas for a while (the same mechanism that makes a flicked page keep scrolling). Your current code just adds up every event it sees, so that momentum tail keeps crossing the threshold and stepping more months. The fix is to lock after one step and only unlock once wheel events actually stop for a bit (real end of gesture, including momentum decay) — not just a fixed cooldown timer.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-13 17:29:07Z)**_

There's no standard, cross-browser way for JS to directly detect "this wheel event is inertial momentum, not the user's finger" — the `WheelEvent` API doesn't expose a momentum-phase flag (Safari's native `NSEvent.momentumPhase` exists at the OS level but isn't surfaced to web content). So we can't detect the tail with certainty, but we can approximate it: momentum events have delta magnitudes that decay from the gesture's peak, so I can ignore events that drop well below the peak seen so far in that swipe — that's the fingerprint of the tail.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-13 17:34:06Z)**_

Implemented and passing typecheck/lint. Behavior now: only one month change fires per swipe (once `WHEEL_STEP_THRESHOLD` is crossed, further events in that same swipe are ignored for stepping purposes), and as soon as an event's magnitude drops to less than `WHEEL_DECAY_RATIO` (50%) of that swipe's peak — the signature of momentum decaying after your fingers lift — tracking resets immediately. No timers involved, so a genuinely new swipe right after can start accumulating again without any artificial delay.

One caveat worth knowing: this is a heuristic, not a guarantee — a very hard, long flick could theoretically still produce a second small resurgence above the new (lower) decay floor before fully dying out, in rare cases. If you see that in testing, `WHEEL_DECAY_RATIO` is the knob to raise (stricter cutoff, ends the gesture sooner) or lower (more lenient). Give it a try.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-13 17:37:09Z)**_

Yes — that's exactly it, and here's why it's not just a tuning problem.

Momentum on a trackpad doesn't start slow and ramp up in a way we could spot early. It starts at roughly whatever velocity your fingers were already moving at the instant they lift, then decays gradually from there. So there's no clean moment where "real finger movement" ends and "tail" begins — the first several tail events look just like continued real scrolling, magnitude-wise. By the time any magnitude-based cutoff (like the decay ratio) is confident enough to call it "tail," a lot of scroll-equivalent distance has already passed through — often enough to cross the step threshold a second time on a good flick.

On top of that: unlike a touchscreen, a laptop trackpad's two-finger scroll never generates a `touchstart`/`touchend`/`pointerup` — the OS just synthesizes `wheel` events, with no signal anywhere in the web platform for "fingers just lifted." So there's no reliable way to detect the true end of your gesture from JS at all, only inference from event timing/magnitude.

Given that, true "one scroll = one change" isn't achievable with certainty — but we can get close with a **fixed lockout after each step** (e.g. ignore all wheel events for ~400-500ms right after a step fires, then reset), instead of the earlier "wait until totally silent" approach that could get extended indefinitely by a long tail. It trades a short, predictable pause after each month-change for much better reliability against double-jumps. Want me to implement that version?

import { useCallback, useRef } from 'react';

export function useResizeObserver<T extends Element>(
  func: (contentRect: DOMRectReadOnly) => void,
): (el: T) => void {
  const observer = useRef<ResizeObserver | undefined>(undefined);
  if (!observer.current) {
    observer.current = new ResizeObserver(entries => {
      func(entries[0].contentRect);
    });
  }

  const elementRef = useCallback((el: T) => {
    observer.current?.disconnect();
    if (el) {
      observer.current?.observe(el, { box: 'border-box' });
    }
  }, []);

  return elementRef;
}
```

  await Promise.all([
    cp(migrationsDir, migrationsDest, { recursive: true }),
    cp(defaultDbPath, path.resolve(publicDataDir, 'default-db.sqlite')),
    cp(sqlWasmPath, path.resolve(publicDir, 'sql-wasm.wasm')),
  ]);

  const entries = await readdir(publicDataDir, {
    recursive: true,
    withFileTypes: true,
  });
  const files = entries
    .filter(e => e.isFile())
    .map(e =>
      path
        .relative(publicDataDir, path.join(e.parentPath, e.name))
        .replaceAll(path.sep, '/'),
    )
    // Skip dotfiles (e.g. legacy `.force-copy-windows` marker). They have no
    // matching extension in the workbox precache globs, so a PWA opened
    // offline would fail to fetch them and break startup (issue #7886).
    .filter(file => !file.split('/').some(part => part.startsWith('.')))
    .sort();
  await writeFile(
    path.resolve(publicDir, 'data-file-index.txt'),
    files.join('\n') + '\n',
  );
}

const lootCoreBackend = (): Plugin => ({
  name: 'loot-core-backend',
  configureServer(server) {
    const child: ChildProcess = spawn(
      'yarn',
      [
        'vite',
        'build',
        '--config',
        lootCoreConfig,
        '--mode',
        'development',
        '--watch',
      ],
      // `shell: true` is required on Windows so the bare `yarn` command
      // resolves to `yarn.cmd` via PATHEXT; without it Node's spawn fails with
      // ENOENT and the loot-core backend (served at /kcab) never builds.
      { cwd: lootCoreRoot, stdio: 'inherit', shell: true },
    );
    child.on('error', err => {
      server.config.logger.error(
        `loot-core backend failed to spawn: ${err.message}`,
      );
    });
    const cleanup = () => {
      if (!child.killed) child.kill('SIGTERM');
    };
    server.httpServer?.once('close', cleanup);
    process.once('SIGINT', cleanup);
    process.once('SIGTERM', cleanup);
    process.once('exit', cleanup);

    server.middlewares.use('/kcab', (req, res, next) => {
      const url = new URL(req.url ?? '/', 'http://localhost');
      const filePath = path.join(lootCoreOutDir, url.pathname);
      if (!filePath.startsWith(lootCoreOutDir + path.sep)) return next();
      const stream = createReadStream(filePath);
      stream
        .on('open', () => {
          res.setHeader(
            'Content-Type',
            CONTENT_TYPES[path.extname(filePath)] ?? 'application/octet-stream',
          );
          stream.pipe(res);
        })
        .on('error', () => next());
    });
  },
  async closeBundle() {
    await mkdir(buildStatsDir, { recursive: true });
    try {
      await rename(
        path.resolve(__dirname, 'build/kcab/stats.json'),
        path.resolve(buildStatsDir, 'loot-core-stats.json'),
      );
    } catch (err) {
      if ((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== 'ENOENT') throw err;
    }
  },
});

const pluginsServiceAssets = (): Plugin => ({
  name: 'plugins-service-assets',
  configureServer(server) {
    server.middlewares.use('/service-worker', (req, res, next) => {
      const url = new URL(req.url ?? '/', 'http://localhost');
      const filePath = path.join(pluginsServiceDistDir, url.pathname);
      if (!filePath.startsWith(pluginsServiceDistDir + path.sep)) return next();
      const stream = createReadStream(filePath);
      stream
        .on('open', () => {
          res.setHeader(
            'Content-Type',
            CONTENT_TYPES[path.extname(filePath)] ?? 'application/octet-stream',
          );
          stream.pipe(res);
        })
        .on('error', () => next());
    });
  },
});

export default defineConfig(async ({ mode, command }) => {
  const env = loadEnv(mode, process.cwd(), '');
  const isVitest = process.env.VITEST === 'true';
  const devHeaders = {
    'Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy': 'same-origin',
    'Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy': 'require-corp',
  };

  // Forward Netlify env variables
  if (process.env.REVIEW_ID) {
    process.env.REACT_APP_REVIEW_ID = process.env.REVIEW_ID;
    process.env.REACT_APP_BRANCH = process.env.BRANCH;
  }

  // Electron packaging (--mode=desktop) bundles loot-core directly, so skip
  // all browser-only staging there.
  if (mode !== 'desktop') {
    if (command === 'build') {
      const stageKcab = build({
        configFile: lootCoreConfig,
        mode: 'production',
        root: lootCoreRoot,
      }).then(async () => {
        const hash = await extractWorkerHash();
        await rm(publicKcabDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
        await cp(lootCoreOutDir, publicKcabDir, { recursive: true });
        return hash;
      });
      const [, , hash] = await Promise.all([
        stagePublicData(),
        stagePluginsService(),
        stageKcab,
      ]);
      process.env.REACT_APP_BACKEND_WORKER_HASH = hash;
    } else {
      await stagePublicData();
      process.env.REACT_APP_BACKEND_WORKER_HASH = 'dev';
    }
  }

  const browserOpen = env.BROWSER_OPEN ? `//${env.BROWSER_OPEN}` : true;

  return {
    base: '/',
    envPrefix: 'REACT_APP_',
    build: {
      minify: 'oxc',
      target: 'es2022',
      sourcemap: true,
      outDir: mode === 'desktop' ? 'build-electron' : 'build',
      assetsDir: 'static',
      manifest: true,
      assetsInlineLimit: 0,
      chunkSizeWarningLimit: 1500,
      rolldownOptions: {
        output: {
          // Users debug from raw stack traces, so compress and strip
          // whitespace but never mangle identifiers (overrides the
          // mangle: true that `minify: 'oxc'` implies).
          minify: {
            compress: true,
            mangle: false,
            codegen: true,
          },
          assetFileNames: (assetInfo: PreRenderedAsset) => {
            const info = assetInfo.name?.split('.') ?? [];
            let extType = info[info.length - 1];
            if (/png|jpe?g|svg|gif|tiff|bmp|ico/i.test(extType)) {
              extType = 'img';
            } else if (/woff|woff2/.test(extType)) {
              extType = 'media';
            }
            return `static/${extType}/[name].[hash][extname]`;
          },
          chunkFileNames: 'static/js/[name].[hash].chunk.js',
          entryFileNames: 'static/js/[name].[hash].js',
        },
      },
    },
    server: {
      host: true,
      headers: devHeaders,
      port: +env.PORT || 5173,
      open: env.BROWSER
        ? ['chrome', 'firefox', 'edge', 'browser', 'browserPrivate'].includes(
            env.BROWSER,
          )
        : browserOpen,
      watch: {
        disableGlobbing: false,
      },
    },
    resolve: {
      ...(mode !== 'browser' && {
        conditions: ['electron-renderer', 'module', 'browser', 'default'],
      }),
      tsconfigPaths: true,
    },
    plugins: [
      // electron (desktop) builds do not support PWA
      mode === 'desktop'
        ? undefined
        : VitePWA({
            registerType: 'prompt',
            // TODO:  The plugin worker build is currently disabled due to issues with offline support. Fix this
            // strategies: 'injectManifest',
            // srcDir: 'service-worker',
            // filename: 'plugin-sw.js',
            // manifest: {
            //   name: 'Actual',
            //   short_name: 'Actual',
            //   description: 'A local-first personal finance tool',
            //   theme_color: '#5c3dbb',
            //   background_color: '#5c3dbb',
            //   display: 'standalone',
            //   start_url: './',
            // },
            // injectManifest: {
            //   maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes: 10 * 1024 * 1024, // 10MB
            //   swSrc: `service-worker/plugin-sw.js`,
            // },
            devOptions: {
              // Disabled: caches stale assets across reloads in dev. Plugin
              // code that explicitly needs a SW can register one itself.
              enabled: false,
              type: 'module',
            },
            workbox: {
              globPatterns: [
                '**/*.{js,css,html,txt,wasm,sql,sqlite,ico,png,woff2,webmanifest}',
              ],
              ignoreURLParametersMatching: [/^v$/],
              navigateFallback: '/index.html',
              maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes: 10 * 1024 * 1024, // 10MB
              navigateFallbackDenylist: [
                /^\/account\/.*$/,
                /^\/admin\/.*$/,
                /^\/secret\/.*$/,
                /^\/openid\/.*$/,
                /^\/plugins\/.*$/,
                /^\/kcab\/.*$/,
                /^\/plugin-data\/.*$/,
                /^\/enablebanking\/.*$/,
              ],
            },
          }),
      injectShims(),
      addWatchers(),
      mode === 'desktop' || isVitest ? undefined : lootCoreBackend(),
      mode === 'desktop' ? undefined : pluginsServiceAssets(),
      react(),
      babel({
        include: [reactCompilerInclude],
        // n.b. Must be a string to ensure plugin resolution order. See https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/pull/5853
        presets: [reactCompilerPreset()],
      }),
      visualizer({
        template: 'raw-data',
        filename: 'build-stats/web-stats.json',
      }),
      !!env.HTTPS && basicSsl(),
    ],
    test: {
      include: ['src/**/*.{test,spec}.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)'],
      environment: 'jsdom',
      globals: true,
      setupFiles: './src/setupTests.ts',
      testTimeout: 10000,
      onConsoleLog(log: string, type: 'stdout' | 'stderr'): boolean | void {
        // print only console.error
        return type === 'stderr';
      },
      maxWorkers: 2,
      reporters: process.env.CI
        ? [
            'default',
            [
              'junit',
              {
                outputFile: './test-results/junit.xml',
                suiteName: 'desktop-client',
              },
            ],
          ]
        : ['default'],
    },
  };
});

import React from 'react';

import { fireEvent, render } from '@testing-library/react';

import { BudgetSummaries } from './BudgetSummaries';
import { MonthsContext } from './MonthsContext';

vi.mock('#hooks/useResizeObserver', () => ({
  useResizeObserver: () => () => {},
}));

vi.mock('.', () => ({
  useBudgetComponents: () => ({
    SummaryComponent: () => null,
  }),
}));

const MONTHS = ['2024-01', '2024-02', '2024-03'];

function renderSummaries(startMonth: string, onMonthSelect: () => void) {
  const { container } = render(
    <MonthsContext.Provider value={{ months: MONTHS, type: 'envelope' }}>
      <BudgetSummaries startMonth={startMonth} onMonthSelect={onMonthSelect} />
    </MonthsContext.Provider>,
  );
  return container.firstChild as HTMLElement;
}

describe('BudgetSummaries wheel navigation', () => {
  test('ignores wheel events where the vertical delta dominates', () => {
    const onMonthSelect = vi.fn();
    const el = renderSummaries('2024-02', onMonthSelect);

    fireEvent.wheel(el, { deltaX: 0, deltaY: 300 });

    expect(onMonthSelect).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  test('steps to the next month once accumulated horizontal delta crosses the threshold', () => {
    const onMonthSelect = vi.fn();
    const el = renderSummaries('2024-02', onMonthSelect);

    fireEvent.wheel(el, { deltaX: 120, deltaY: 0 });
    expect(onMonthSelect).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

    fireEvent.wheel(el, { deltaX: 120, deltaY: 0 });
    expect(onMonthSelect).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(onMonthSelect).toHaveBeenCalledWith('2024-03');
  });

  test('steps to the previous month on a negative horizontal swipe', () => {
    const onMonthSelect = vi.fn();
    const el = renderSummaries('2024-02', onMonthSelect);

    fireEvent.wheel(el, { deltaX: -220, deltaY: 0 });

    expect(onMonthSelect).toHaveBeenCalledWith('2024-01');
  });

  test('locks out further steps for a fixed window after a step fires', () => {
    const onMonthSelect = vi.fn();
    const el = renderSummaries('2024-02', onMonthSelect);

    fireEvent.wheel(el, { deltaX: 220, deltaY: 0 });
    expect(onMonthSelect).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);

    // Date.now() is frozen in tests (see setupTests.ts), so these extra
    // events land within the lockout window — standing in for a swipe's
    // trailing momentum, which should not trigger extra steps.
    fireEvent.wheel(el, { deltaX: 220, deltaY: 0 });
    fireEvent.wheel(el, { deltaX: 220, deltaY: 0 });

    expect(onMonthSelect).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  test('allows another step once the lockout window has elapsed', () => {
    const onMonthSelect = vi.fn();
    const el = renderSummaries('2024-02', onMonthSelect);

    fireEvent.wheel(el, { deltaX: 220, deltaY: 0 });
    expect(onMonthSelect).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);

    const originalNow = Date.now;
    Date.now = () => originalNow() + 1000;
    try {
      fireEvent.wheel(el, { deltaX: 220, deltaY: 0 });
    } finally {
      Date.now = originalNow;
    }

    expect(onMonthSelect).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(onMonthSelect).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('2024-03');
  });
});

# Writing Release Notes for actualbudget/actual

Release notes are the user-facing changelog. Each code change adds one Markdown file to `upcoming-release-notes/`, and these get collected into the published changelog at the next release. The authoritative source is the **Writing Good Release Notes** section of `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md`. Read it if anything below is unclear.

## The file

Create `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is a **short, descriptive kebab-case slug** naming the change (e.g. `add-payee-autocomplete.md`, `fix-mobile-category-delete.md`). Do **not** use a PR number, since the PR link is resolved automatically at release time. (Numeric filenames like `1234.md` still work, but a slug is preferred.)

```markdown
---
category: Features
authors: [YourGitHubUsername]
---

Add payee autocomplete to the transaction entry form
```

- **`category`**: exactly one of `Features` (new feature), `Enhancements` (improvement to an existing feature), `Bugfix` (bug fix), or `Maintenance` (internal change with no user-visible effect).
- **`authors`**: array of the GitHub username(s) who did the work.

## Writing the entry

The body is the changelog line. It is read by everyday users, not developers.

- **One sentence.** Short and clear. No paragraphs, no bullet lists, no long prose.
- **Plain language, no technical detail.** Describe what changed for the user, not how it was built. Avoid file names, function names, internal component names, and implementation jargon. (Exception: `Maintenance` entries may be technical, since they are for internal changes.)
- **Phrase it as a command.** Start with a present-tense verb: "Add …", "Fix …", "Show …", not "Added …" or "Adds …".
- Generally match the PR title, but reword it if that reads more clearly to a user.

Good: `Fix incorrect balance when reconciling an account with future transactions`
Too technical: `Fix off-by-one in reconcileTransactions() when txn.date > today`
